assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete choice made dynamic programming empirically operational across major economic applications.
assessment.attribution: Rust is the central foundational contributor; the broader listed programme has important subsequent contributors.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding, extensively used, and have demonstrated durable influence.
uncertainties: The appropriate boundary between the original framework and later structural-estimation advances remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern quantitative thinking about trade and its welfare consequences.
assessment.attribution: Melitz provides the defining heterogeneous-firm framework, while the wider intellectual lineage includes several related trade contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been central to trade research and applied policy analysis for two decades.
uncertainties: Separating the credited contribution from adjacent foundational trade work is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework supplied a coherent modern account of monetary-policy transmission and stabilization.
assessment.attribution: Woodford, Gali, and Calvo represent central theoretical elements, but the listed contribution is unusually collective and overlaps with other foundational work.
assessment.maturity: Its influence on macroeconomic research and monetary-policy practice is deep and well established.
uncertainties: The appropriate laureate set is highly contested given the many indispensable contributors.
The scope combines nominal-rigidity theory, monetary policy, and a broader framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods gave empirical economists broadly applicable tools for persistent-panel settings.
assessment.attribution: The three credited researchers have a closely connected and identifiable contribution.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been tested, taught, and used across empirical fields for decades.
uncertainties: Their broad methodological importance must be weighed against whether it constitutes a sufficiently unified scientific discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed the treatment of inference when data and assumptions cannot support point identification.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the principal foundational figure; subsequent developments materially extended the programme.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature, influential, and has reshaped standards for credible empirical conclusions.
uncertainties: The candidate description spans several related methodological contributions with different coauthor roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models connect distributional heterogeneity to aggregate policy transmission in a consequential way.
assessment.attribution: Moll, Violante, and Kaplan are strongly associated with the modern quantitative framework, though it draws on a substantial heterogeneous-agent macro literature.
assessment.maturity: The programme has rapidly become influential and has generated a large applied literature.
uncertainties: The framework is comparatively recent relative to the most mature candidates.
Its eventual empirical and policy durability remains to be assessed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The combination of theory and measurement substantially advanced understanding of adverse selection in insurance markets.
assessment.attribution: The listed researchers form a plausible core, although the theoretical and empirical strands have distinct intellectual origins.
assessment.maturity: The work has proved influential in health, insurance, and public-economics research.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is best viewed as one sufficiently unified discovery is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data opened a powerful empirical programme on intergenerational mobility and the role of place.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are major architects of the research programme, with other listed contributors also important.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has already influenced economic research and public debate substantially.
uncertainties: The work is newer than several leading candidates.
Interpretation of descriptive mobility patterns and causal mechanisms remains an active research area.
